'''Vitaly N. Efimov''' (Russian: Вита́лий Никола́евич Ефи́мов; born 1938) is a Soviet [[theoretical physicist]]. He proposed the existence of a novel and exotic state of matter now dubbed the [[Efimov State]] as a researcher in [[Ioffe Institute|A. F. Ioffe Physico-Technical Institute]], [[USSR Academy of Sciences]], [[Leningrad]], [[USSR]] in his 1970 paper "Energy levels arising from resonant two-body forces in a three-body system".<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Efimov | first1 = V. | author-link1 = Vitaly Efimov| doi = 10.1016/0370-2693(70)90349-7 | title = Energy levels arising from resonant two-body forces in a three-body system | journal = [[Physics Letters B]]| volume = 33 | issue = 8 | pages = 563–564 | year = 1970 |bibcode = 1970PhLB...33..563E }}</ref> It was announced in 2006 that the existence of this state of matter had been confirmed.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/nature04626| pmid = 16541068| title = Evidence for Efimov quantum states in an ultracold gas of caesium atoms| journal = [[Nature (journal)|Nature]]| volume = 440| issue = 7082| pages = 315–8| year = 2006| last1 = Kraemer | first1 = T.| last2 = Mark | first2 = M.| last3 = Waldburger | first3 = P.| last4 = Danzl | first4 = J. G.| last5 = Chin | first5 = C.| last6 = Engeser | first6 = B.| last7 = Lange | first7 = A. D.| last8 = Pilch | first8 = K.| last9 = Jaakkola | first9 = A.| last10 = Nägerl | first10 = H. -C. | last11 = Grimm | first11 = R. | author-link11 = Rudolf Grimm| arxiv = cond-mat/0512394 | bibcode = 2006Natur.440..315K| s2cid = 4379828}}</ref>

Formerly an affiliate professor of physics at the [[University of Washington]], he is now a lecturer emeritus.<ref>https://phys.washington.edu/people/vitaly-efimov</ref>

In 2018, he has been selected as the winner of the Inaugural Fadeev Medal.<ref>[https://www.aps.org/units/gfb/awards/faddeev-medal.cfm ''  Faddeev Medal ''].</ref>
